column2: Subhadra and Vibhadra, Sunanda, Pushpananda, Jaya and Vijaya, Kumbha, Purna, and Uttara —
the nine treasure-pots in order: Purna and Uttara. Having first given the seat, striking and drawing with the arrow-atom,
covering all without distinction with armor; with clay, cow-dung, cow-urine decoctions and scented water,
one should perform the cleansing bath with the weapon-mantra ending in hum phat; by rule the bath with the five cow-products and the five nectars;
one should next make the scented-water bath with the atom marked with one's own name; then with water from fruits, jewels, gold and cow-horns,
having smeared with sandal one should cover the stone with cloths; having given a seat made of gold and led it around the sacrifice in circumambulation,
one should place it on a bed or a couch of kusha with the heart-mantra. Having worshipped and placed the collection of principles from intellect to earth,
one should place in order the three pervading principles of the three sections. From intellect to mind, to anxiety and subtle elements,
from subtle elements to earth the stations of Shiva, knowledge and Self; one should worship the principles with their own mantras and the lords of principles with the heart-mantra

in places marked with flower garlands and the like in order: "Om Hum, homage to the Shiva-principle; Om Hum, homage to Rudra, lord of the Shiva-principle; Om Ham, homage to the knowledge-principle; Om Ham, homage to Vishnu, lord of the knowledge-principle; Om Ham, homage to the Self-principle; Om Ham, homage to Brahma, lord of the Self-principle" — earth, fire, sacrificer, sun, water, wind, moon and space.
For each principle one should place eight forms on each stone: Sarva, Pashupati, Ugra, Rudra, Bhava, Ishvara,
Mahadeva and Bhima, and the lords of the forms in order: "Om, homage to the Earth form; Om, homage to the lord of earth" and so on; the guardians of the world with their own atoms in number,
having placed one should worship the pots with those mantras or with one's own atoms. The seed-syllables of Indra and the others in the order to be told:
Lum Rum Shum Pum Vum Yum Mum Hum Kshum — thus the nine-stone side is stated, and the five-station stone. One should place the forms for each principle; in creation the five from earth onward:
Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, Ishvara and Sadashiva — these five lords of forms are to be worshipped in them as before.

Om, homage to the Earth form; Om, homage to Brahma, lord of the Earth form and so on — the mantras; having worshipped the five pots in order by their own names, one should enclose by rule; the placing from the middle stone onward.
One should make the enclosure with the rampart mantra with ash and darbha; having placed the supporting power in the pits, having worshipped, one should satisfy
the principles, the lords of principles, forms and lords of forms with ghee and the rest. Then for the purification of the Brahma-part, in order with the root and limbs with Brahmas,
having done from a hundred to full, one should sprinkle the stones with peace-waters; one should worship, touching with kusha, each principle in order.
Having done presence and connection one should place again pure. Thus having gone to and fro one should perform the work in the three sections.

Om Am Im, homage to the Self-principle and the knowledge-principle — one should touch with darbha-root and the rest the three beginning with the Brahma-limb in order. One should do the connection of principles with short and long application.

Om Ham Um, homage to the knowledge-principle and Shiva-principle. Copper pots filled with ghee and honey, with jewels, sprinkled with arghya of the five cow-products, presiding deities of the world-guardians,
having worshipped with their own mantras one should perform the oblation in their presence. Then one should recall the presiding deities of all stones:

of the form of knowledge, bathed, golden-colored, clad in stones; for removing faults of deficiency and the rest and for purifying the building site, one should offer with the weapon-mantra up to the head a hundred and a hundred oblations.
Brahma has sixty-four squares; Marichi and the other deities, fifty-four squares... in the eight with flavor-fire;
Ishana and others nine squares; Skanda and others are the Shaktis; Charaki and the others likewise; ropes, bamboo and the rest as before.
It is to be known with a thousand bamboos, with squares going into the site-mandala; the placing there should be ninefold by one who knows the regional site.
The site of twenty-five squares called Vaitala is remembered on the earth; another is nine-squared, and another sixteen-footed.
In the middle of the six-angled, three-angled, round and the rest there should be a four-sided one. In digging equal to the site, on the back, in the placing with the Brahma stone,
in the entry of the seed and in the installation of an image, one should offer porridge as food to all.
In what is stated and unstated, the site by the measure of five cubits; the house-temple measure; the site is always best.
Above one should contemplate Brahma and the pervading Maheshvara; in these the support, in the middle of the sky-temple.
Having given an offering one should repeat the weapon-mantra, removing obstacle-faults. Even in the five-stone case a little is taught as follows:
In the middle the full stone placed, half in the Subhadra pot; Nanda and the rest on the lotuses and the like in the corners, fire and the others in order;
in the absence of the middle, the four are held in the feeling of mothers: "Om Purna, you, of the great universe, bearing the mark of the collection of all,
make all complete here, daughter of Angiras. Om Nanda, you gladden men; I establish you here;
stay in the temple, satisfied, as long as moon, sun and stars; Nanda, give life, desire and fortune, O Vasishtha, to the embodied.
In this temple protection is to be made always by you with effort. Om Bhadra, always make good for the worlds, Kashyapi.
Giver of life, giver of desire, goddess, be ever giver of fortune. Om Jaya, here always, goddess, be giver of fortune and life.
Om Jaya, here always, goddess, stay, established by me; be always mistress for victory and prosperity, Bhargavi.
Om Rikta, destroying excess faults, giver of accomplishment and liberation, auspicious, ever and everywhere, stay in this, of universal form."
Having meditated on the sky-temple, one should place the three principles there. Then having made the expiatory oblation one should dismiss the sacrifice by rule.
The six-angled for Vayu, a lotus in the north, an eight-angled for Shiva; the pit dug slantwise for Shiva, above with the girdle.
Outside it are three girdles with finger-measures of Veda, fire and Yama; or one of six fingers; the girdles are of the shape of the pit.
Above them is the yoni, in the middle shaped like a pipal leaf; a finger in height, eight fingers in breadth;
length by half the pit-measure; the lower equal to the pit's neck. For the east, southeast and south pits the yoni faces north;
of the rest it faces east; in the northeast, either of the two. The twenty-fourth part of the pits is called a finger — thus.
Arches of plaksha, udumbara, kashtha-ashvattha and banyan, in order, named Shanti, Bhuti, Bala, Arogya and so on in order.
Five, six and seven cubits, and standing in a cubit-pit, half the breadth, adorned with mango leaves and the like.
A banner like Indra's bow, red, black, smoky, moon-bright, white-hued and golden, like crystal.
In the east and others lotus-born red; blue for Ananta in the southwest. Five cubits and half; banners long and wide;
staffs of a cubit, for banners of five cubits; from an anthill, the tip of an elephant tusk, a bull's horn,
a lotus-bed, a boar, a cowpen, a crossroads — twelve clays are to be taken; for Vaikuntha eight; for Pinaki.
Born from the bark of banyan, udumbara, ashvattha, mango and jambu: five astringents are to be taken, and eight seasonal fruits;
waters from holy places, fragrant ones, and the water of all herbs. I shall tell the praised flowers and fruits, and jewels and cow-horn water.
One should bring for bathing the five, and the nectar of the five cow-products; flour-made cloth and other materials for cleansing;
a pot with a thousand holes for the circle, and rochana; a hundred roots of herbs: Vijaya, Lakshmana, Bala,
Guduchi, Atibala, Patha, Sahadeva, Shatavari, Riddhi, Suvarchasa, Vriddhi, each told for the bath.
For protection, a mass of sesame and darbha, and ash-bath alone; powders of barley, wheat and bilva by the wise;
ointment with camphor; pots of rhinoceros horn for bathing; a bedstead and a pair of mattresses with pillow and cloth,
one should make according to means in arranging the bed with marks. One should make a vessel with ghee and honey and a golden rod,
the Vardhani and Shiva's pot and the world-guardians' pots; one pot for sleep, for peace by the number of pits;
the pots of door-guards and Dharma and so on and Prashanta; and other pots of Vastu, Lakshmi and Ganesha,
supported on heaps of grain, clothed, adorned with garlands, with gold, anointed, filled with scent and water,
with full vessels and fruit stands, with leaves and the like, with marks; one should cover the pots with cloth and bring white mustard
for scattering, and parched grain, and the sword of knowledge as before; a porridge-vessel with lid and a copper ladle,
a vessel with ghee and honey for anointing the feet; seats of three hundred darbha leaves, arm-length,
four and four likewise; palasha enclosing sticks also; a sesame vessel, an offering vessel, an arghya vessel, a thread;
a pot of fruits of twenty-eight measures, incense giver; ladles, a basket, a seat, a fan, dry fuel;
flower, leaf, guggulu, ghee lamps and incense; rice, three-strand cord, cow-products, ghee, barley, sesame;
kusha for peace, the three sweets, fuel sticks of ten joints; a ladle of arm-length, a hand — for peace with the sun and other planets;
fuel sticks born of arka and palasha, khadira, apamarga and pippala, udumbara, shami, durva and kusha — a hundred and eight;
in their absence barley and sesame; likewise household implements; a pot, ladle, lid and the like; two pieces of cloth to the gods and others;
seal, crown, garments, necklaces, earrings and bracelets one should make for worship of the teacher; one should avoid miserliness.
Worship of the image-bearers and weapon-reciters, a quarter less by foot, would be equal to that of the reciters, Brahmins, astrologers and craftsmen.
For peace of the thunderbolt and sun: sapphire, great sapphire, pearls, flower and lotus rubies and lapis lazuli, jewel the eighth;
vetiver, madhava, krantara, red sandal, agaru, shrikhanda, sarika, kushtha, shankhini — the quality of herbs.
Gold, copper, red, silver with bronze, and lead — thus the metals; orpiment, realgar,
red ochre, gold pyrite, mercury, fire-ochre, sulfur and mica — thus eight minerals; and grains likewise.
One should bring wheat with sesame, beans, mung and barley, wild rice, millet; thus eight grains are declared.
